low.note: Need more leads for a rental to pencil. Treat volume bands one tier stricter (e.g. mid volume reads as low).

mid.note: Standard local services. Prefer mid+ cluster volume unless SERP is unusually soft.

high.note: Specialty / high-ticket (trenchless, foundation, major HVAC replacement, etc.). Use volume bands below as written.

volumeMetric.definition: Sum of Google Ads Keyword Planner monthly volumes for the selected keyword set, measured per city geo that exists in Google Ads, then summed across the cluster. Not rough geo-phrase ranges on geo-suffixed phrases.
interpretationNotes: primaryVolume = searches FROM the primary city geo, not searches about that city.
clusterSum adds independent city geos; it does not double-count the same search.
Ads volumes are bucketed (10, 20, 30, 50…). Local niches are noisy at the low end.
null means insufficient data; 0 means measured zero.
Ads competition / CPC are auction metrics, not organic SEO difficulty. High CPC can signal commercial intent.

authorityMetric.name: DataForSEO Rank
authorityMetric.disclaimer: DataForSEO Rank is a backlink-based authority score. It is NOT Moz Domain Authority or Ahrefs Domain Rating. Use it for relative competitor comparison only.

low.label: Low
low.howToTreat: Only pursue if job value is high AND SERP is soft. Thin demand; ranking cannot invent leads.

mid.label: Mid
mid.howToTreat: Default worth-a-closer-look band for specialty trades.

high.label: High
high.howToTreat: Strong local demand for a specialty niche if competition is not locked up.

very_high.label: Very high
very_high.howToTreat: Excellent demand — score competition harder; expect stronger Map Pack + organic sites.

competitionScore.definition: 1–10 opportunity score from organic SERP softness. Higher = easier / more opportunity (not 'more competitors'). Based on unique organic service domains in the top results after stripping directories.

homepageAdjustment.note: Dedicated niche/homepages are harder to displace than location sub-pages. Cap score at 1 minimum.

medianDomainRankAdjustment.note: After Stage 2 enrichment: median competitor DataForSEO domain Rank ≥40 → harder (−1); median <20 → easier (+1). Cap 1–10.

mapPackGapScore.definition: 1–10 opportunity from Map Pack gap. Higher = more gap (easier path or clearer blue-link focus).

absent.label: Map Pack absent — stronger early opportunity for a new site + later GBP.

present.label: Map Pack present — blue-link / organic path first; Map Pack usually needs a real GBP.

jobValueScore.definition: 1–10 from estimated average job cost. Filled by Claude/human — DataForSEO does not produce this.

displaceability.definition: 1–10 how displaceable organic blue-link competitors look for a new niche homepage. Higher = easier to outrank over time. This is NOT a promise of ranking in 4–6 months.
displaceability.honestyLimit: Scores page thinness + relative DataForSEO Rank. Human/Claude may confirm; do not invent Rank or word counts.

aggregateHints.mostlyThinStubs: Most URLs look like thin location/service stubs → lean pursue even at mid proposedScore.
aggregateHints.severalStrongPages: Several strong niche pages on higher-Rank domains → deprioritize.

soft.note: Few or no dedicated niche sites; mostly directories or thin sub-pages.

hard.note: Map Pack filled with strong locals and/or several dedicated niche sites.

proposedScoreWeights.note: When displaceability is null (Stage 1 only), renormalize the other four weights to sum to 1. Round to 1 decimal. Do not invent missing jobValue — leave proposedScore null until jobValue is set.

decisionRulesSpecialtyHighTicket.summary: Mid+ volume + mixed SERP + high displaceability (mostly thin stubs) → pursue.
Mid volume + mixed SERP + low displaceability (strong niche pages) → deprioritize.
Mid volume + hard SERP → pass or deprioritize.
Low volume + soft SERP + very high job value → maybe, as a portfolio bet.
Low volume without a soft-SERP + high-ticket exception → pass.
High volume + hard SERP → do not chase unless you have a real GBP / contractor angle.
Mixed signals — human review using scoreInputs, enrichment pages, and SERP links.

pathToWin.siteOnlyDefinition: Site-only = a Rank & Rent website without a strong Google Business Profile (often no GBP at launch).

twoLanes.mapPack: The 3 local businesses with the map. Google heavily favors GBP: reviews, address/NAP, categories, proximity, profile activity.
twoLanes.blueLinks: Normal organic results under/around the pack. Google favors web pages: relevance, content, internal links, backlinks.

pathToWin.blueLinksFirst: A new Rank & Rent site usually starts site-only, so it generally cannot win the Map Pack early. It can rank in blue links first—especially when competitors only have thin location sub-pages and no dedicated niche homepage. Map Pack becomes realistic after a renter attaches a real GBP.
playbook: Build the site and aim to rank in organic blue links to get leads.
Rent to a contractor who has or will create a real GBP.
Push Map Pack as a second phase once the GBP is attached.
pathToWin.mapPackAbsent: Stronger early opportunity: blue links face less local-pack squeeze; later GBP can compete in both lanes.
pathToWin.mapPackPresent: Expect to compete below the pack first. Soft organic (0–1 niche homepages, sub-pages only) still supports a site-only build.

enrichmentGate.note: Stage 2 --enrich is recommended when Stage 1 demand is mid+ and decision is review/pursue/maybe. Always available via explicit --enrich / enrich-candidate.
